candidate.title: Nextera™ Rapid Capture
candidate.scope: The single Nextera Rapid Capture enrichment route depicted in the assigned Illumina schematic: already denatured and pooled Nextera library fragments undergo probe hybridization, capture on streptavidin magnetic beads, and elution to a product labeled ready for cluster generation. The input preparation history is preserved without inventing upstream library-preparation operations. No alternative workflow or branch is drawn; cluster generation is the downstream interface, not a depicted operation. The catalogue supplies only the product name and no primary-paper association.

states.label: Denatured and pooled fragments from Nextera library
features: The input is an already prepared, denatured, pooled library, drawn as multiple separate linear fragments.
One representative fragment has a central segment labeled Target and colored flanking regions; the starting pool has not yet undergone the depicted capture.
The specimen and biological origin of the target sequence are not identified in this panel.

evidence.locator: Top input region: Target above a colored fragment and the label Denatured and pooled fragments from Nextera library

states.label: Biotinylated target probe
features: A short dark-blue probe carries a small attached symbol and is explicitly labeled biotinylated.
The probe is added to the library pool at the plus sign; its later attachment to the target region is shown without a probe sequence or chemical structure.

evidence.locator: Upper-middle region: plus sign, short blue probe with attached symbol, and Biotinylated target probe label

states.label: Library fragment hybridized to a biotinylated target probe
features: The long library fragment retains its colored flanks and central target segment.
A shorter blue probe is paired beneath the central target segment and retains its attached biotin symbol.

evidence.locator: Hybridize probes to targets region: long library strand paired centrally with short blue biotinylated probe

states.label: Streptavidin magnetic bead capture reagent
features: The capture panel depicts a gray bead surface bearing blue binding components, with the caption identifying streptavidin magnetic beads.
The bead is a capture support that becomes part of the attached complex; its drawing does not specify a molecular structure or a separate magnetic-separation operation.

evidence.locator: Capture on streptavidin magnetic beads region: gray bead surface with blue surface components

states.label: Bead-attached probe–target library complex
features: The target-containing library fragment remains paired with its probe and retains its flanking library regions.
The probe-associated biotin symbol contacts a blue component on the streptavidin magnetic bead, placing the library fragment in a bead-attached state.

evidence.locator: Capture panel: long colored fragment above a short blue probe joined through its attached symbol to the bead surface

states.label: Eluted target-containing library product ready for cluster generation
features: The bottom product is drawn as a free linear library fragment without the probe or bead attached.
Visible features run left to right as P5, Index 2, Target, Index 1, and P7; the target and both index regions remain on the same depicted library fragment.
P5 and P7 are the depicted library-end labels; the panel does not label chemical 5′ or 3′ end groups.

evidence.locator: Bottom product: P5, Index 2, Target, Index 1, P7 and Product ready for cluster generation

operations.label: Hybridize probes to targets
operations.description: Combine the already denatured, pooled library fragments with biotinylated target probes. The depicted output differs from the input library by having a short probe paired to the central target segment of a library fragment.
operations.mechanism: Probe–target hybridization, as named by the caption and drawn as a short probe paired with the target region.
operations.information_effect: Probe binding associates the capture handle with a target-bearing library molecule while preserving that molecule's flanking library regions. The target sequence is carried by the library fragment, rather than being replaced by a newly synthesized probe product.

evidence.locator: Input fragments plus biotinylated target probe, downward arrow, and Hybridize probes to targets output

operations.label: Capture on streptavidin magnetic beads
operations.description: Attach the hybridized probe–library complex to the streptavidin magnetic bead support. The library fragment changes from a soluble probe-bound complex to a bead-attached complex; the long target-bearing fragment and its library flanks remain drawn intact.
operations.mechanism: Capture through the biotinylated probe at the streptavidin bead surface. This linkage is interpreted from the biotinylated-probe label, streptavidin-bead caption, and drawn probe-to-bead connection.
operations.information_effect: This is a target-enrichment selection: hybridization connects a target-containing library fragment to the capture support. The schematic supplies no measured enrichment efficiency or basis for assuming perfect on-target specificity.

evidence.locator: Arrow from Hybridize probes to targets to Capture on streptavidin magnetic beads and the attached complex
Biotinylated target probe label and capture-panel probe-to-bead connection
evidence.rationale: The separately labeled biotinylated probe remains paired to the library and is drawn connected to the labeled streptavidin bead. Together these features support affinity capture mediated by the probe's biotin and enrichment of probe-bound library molecules; they do not quantify specificity.

operations.label: Elute
operations.description: Release the target-containing library fragment from the bead-associated capture complex into the free product shown at the bottom. The product retains the central target and flanking index/end regions and is labeled ready for cluster generation.
operations.information_effect: The output library physically carries the selected target sequence together with Index 2 and Index 1. Downstream sequencing could therefore read sequence represented by the recovered library; no sequence data or quantitative biological measurement is produced within this schematic. The panel does not define the index-to-sample mapping or establish a cell-specific barcode.

evidence.rationale: The drawn target and index regions remain on a library molecule labeled ready for cluster generation, supporting a sequence-bearing downstream library interface. A ready library alone does not establish an observed sequence, abundance estimate, index assignment, or single-cell identity.

Denaturation and pooling are stated properties of the starting library; upstream Nextera library preparation and downstream cluster generation are outside the shown transformations. checks.rationale: Independently inspected the complete attached diagram and supplied catalogue text. The candidate covers every shown transformation: library plus probe hybridization, bead capture, and elution. Its six states, three local operations, and eight material flows agree at both ends of every interface. The two multi-input operations are genuine combinations: the plus sign joins library and probe, and bead capture produces an attached complex. There are no independent processing branches, alternatives, compartments, or data-integration operations to restore. The target-containing library fragment remains the product carrier, rather than a newly synthesized probe product. The final P5/Index 2/Target/Index 1/P7 labels, probe biotin, and bead attachment/release are retained. The candidate avoids claiming perfect specificity, cell identity, observed sequencing results, or a particular elution mechanism. No publication is supplied or required by the caller; empty paper_matches does not imply full-text verification. There is no consequential source conflict, unsupported correction, or architecture-changing unknown requiring revision or research.
